title: NETWORKING ESSENTIALS
subtitle: How a request travels from a user to your service, and which protocol to pick for which job.
footer: System Design, Step by Step · core concepts

items: DNS resolves the name; an L4 load balancer forwards TCP connections without reading them. Very fast, good for WebSockets and raw TCP.
An L7 load balancer reads HTTP and routes by path, header, or cookie; it terminates TLS and can do sticky sessions.

head: Protocol
Use
rows: Fallback push when nothing else works

items: Public API used by browsers and partners: REST over HTTPS.
High-volume calls between internal services: gRPC.
Server pushes a stream to the client: SSE.
Routing by URL path, header or cookie: L7 load balancer. Raw TCP or very high throughput: L4.

blocks.text: "Clients talk REST through an L7 load balancer; internal services use gRPC. Live updates go over SSE, which reconnects automatically."
